# the contributor audit: sampled majorants, marked entropy and regular contact allocations

the contributor fully read the following three sources:

- `candidate 87de5b3c068291f1`;
- `candidate 0e1bf4bac5d35265`;
- `candidate 7ed1287ead37cfb6`.

All three pass within their stated hypotheses. They concern actual mixed-volume rows and fixed old integer-base marks. They do not supply the sharp body inequality required for OC.

## Sampled touching planes and the fixed-mark lower bound

For an own-interior mark, a continuous-coordinate supergradient is bounded by the positive function's sampled maximum divided by the fixed interior radius. The sampled array phi_z=max(U-c.X) satisfies every anchored concavity inequality. Finite Farkas therefore supplies a base slope touching phi at the marked base. This is valid even at a projection boundary where an ambient supporting affine function need not exist.

The minimum-norm feasible base slope is uniformly bounded because the base matrix is fixed. The source proves this directly: the projection normal lies in the cone of active constraint normals, a linearly independent active subset suffices, and the resulting finite list of pseudoinverse formulas gives a uniform bound. No full-dimensional base assumption or strict feasibility is needed.

The minimum of the finitely many planes dominates the current parameter on sampled fibers and agrees with it at all old marks. Every subsequential plane limit dominates old L, touches its certificate marks, and hence equals L on all sampled fibers by the global multiplicative certificate. Thus these majorants, unlike the original varying parameters, converge uniformly through the sampled boundaries and have a common positive floor.

The exact comparison is

    sum sigma_i log(U_t(Y_i)/L_i)
       >= M^(-1)[integral_old log V_t-integral_current log V_t].

The current integral is nonnegative by domination of the normalized U_t. Replacing log V_t by the fixed continuous log L on the O(t) symmetric difference costs o(t). The signed shell formula therefore gives the coefficient s(v)=M^(-1) integral_boundary log L v, at the unchanged old marks. No source displacement, parameter derivative or boundary convergence of U_t is used. the contributor reran **18,641 exact calibration checks**, including the nonzero signed translation coefficient.

## Marked entropy and its exact finite-dimensional derivative

For H_C(b)=sup mean_old log U subject to U(Y_i)<=b_i, the old certificate gives H_C(l)=0 and uniqueness of the sampled maximizer L. The important compactness estimate requires no optimizer continuity: contract each tilted row toward its own conditional fiber mean. This preserves its full barycenter exactly and maps it into any sufficiently nearby actual body. Concavity and positivity bound each sampled maximum by the finite marked upper bounds, since the row densities sum to the entire old volume target on any fixed inner core.

Near-maximizing entropy parameters have maxima also bounded away from zero on each fiber. Their logarithms are uniformly integrable by the homothetic superlevel estimate. Replacing them with the bounded sampled majorants preserves feasibility and increases entropy. Any limiting majorant is old-feasible with entropy at least zero, so the certificate equality case forces it to be L on S. This proves a common positive floor and local positive attainment by a finite-plane representative. The diagonal argument for nearby problems does not assume global positive attainment for arbitrary marked data.

These representatives extend to both old and current hulls. Comparing the two actual optimizers gives

    H_t(b(t)) = H_C(b(t)) - t s(v) + o(t).

The denominator here is the fixed old M. The current denominator changes no first-order coefficient at the old zero entropy value.

The entire superdifferential of the finite concave function H_C at l is precisely {sigma_i/l_i}, over all old contact certificate weight vectors. One inclusion follows from the global logarithmic inequality. Conversely, a supergradient is nonnegative by monotonicity, satisfies sum g_i l_i=1 by the exact scaling law, and its inequalities for affine and negative convex parameter tests yield the finite-source martingale to dm/(ML). Equal L moments then make the rows L-tight. Consequently

    H_t(l+t h+o(t))
       = t[-s(v)+min_certificates sum sigma_i h_i/l_i]+o(t),

with an attained minimum over the compact set of certificate weights. This is the marked entropy value derivative. It is not an asserted derivative of optimized buffered depth; movement of deepest marks and actual cap inverses remain distinct issues.

## Piecewise analytic allocation

The feasible finite row-moment range is compact by weak-star compactness. A relative-boundary supporting functional is an array of affine scores. Its exposed face is exactly the moment range obtained by allowing only pointwise maximizing labels: the support gap is an integral of a nonnegative function. Hence finite facial reduction lowers affine dimension until the target lies in the relative interior. Whole-fiber affine ties retain every tied label.

On the final allowed label sets, log-sum-exp differs from the support function by at most nu(S) log(number of labels). The entropy dual is coercive on span(D-D), and its genuine gauge is the perpendicular space. Its attained minimizer gives exact row moments by the gradient equation. On every cell the allocation is an affine softmax; after refining by the PL cells of L, its tilted density is analytic with bounded derivatives. The assertions are instance-specific and permit jumps across internal affine interfaces.

The interval example proves that global continuity cannot be required. This regular allocation theorem is valid, but is not needed for the simpler sampled-majorant lower bound. No physical compatibility is inferred from pushing its rows.

Full OC remains unproved. These results remove parameter compactness and fixed-mark boundary bookkeeping obstacles; they do not establish a Gamma payment or identify volume and surface transports.
